--- PART 1/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "Parent was slot4 with fitness 246.22. Some slots higher: slot11 259.86, slot3 254.29, slot2 253.70, slot5 249.34, slot4 246.22. Need improve."
STRATEGY: Parent is slot4, a conditional cooperator/retaliator in an iterated PD tournament. The trace simulates the 12 population strategies and their payoffs against candidate behaviours. It plans a new strategy that cooperates initially, retaliates against defection, and defects on the last round.

--- PART 2/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "Given the fitness values, the best strategies (S11, S3, S2) are all variants of TFT with forgiveness and some end-game tweaks. S11 got 259.86. To beat it, we need to score higher against the population."
STRATEGY: The parent is a candidate TFT-with-last-round-defection strategy being evaluated against a fixed population of 12 opponents. The trace simulates that candidate against S1, S2, S3, S5, S10 and others, then considers a probe-then-adapt variant that defects on round 2 and adapts to the opponent's response. The proposed change is to add an early probe defection and exploit forgiving opponents while avoiding being classified as always-cooperate.

--- PART 3/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given the complexity, maybe the best approach is to write a strategy that is a well-known robust strategy like "Pavlov" or "Tit-for-Tat with forgiveness and occasional probing". But we need to beat 259.86."
STRATEGY: The parent is a strategy being revised to beat a fitness threshold of 259.86. The trace simulates candidate strategies (Probe-TFT, Forgiving TFT, adaptive probe/exploit) against opponents S0–S11. It changes the strategy by adding an early probe, forgiveness, exploit mode, and last-round defection.

--- PART 4/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "So our exploit mode is good against S0." / "So our strategy does exactly that: if opp_def_count > 0, we go to forgiving TFT."
STRATEGY: The parent is a forgiving TFT-style strategy that cooperates unless the opponent defects twice in a row, with an early probe and end-game defection. The trace simulates this parent against S0, S3, S5, S10, and S11, and also simulates variants such as defecting every 6 rounds, probing at round 2, and switching to forgiving TFT after retaliation. It proposes changing the parent to a more adaptive probing strategy: probe early, continue scheduled exploitation if the opponent does not retaliate, and switch to conservative forgiving TFT if the opponent retaliates.

--- PART 5/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given the analysis, I think the best strategy is a forgiving TFT with an early probe and a final-round defection"
STRATEGY: Parent is a forgiving TFT with an early probe and final-round defection; simulated against S0–S11 and archive; changed by adding an exploit mode that defects every 6 rounds when the opponent has never defected, plus endgame defection.
